direct_answer: Aker BP integrates sustainability-related performance into its variable remuneration (bonus) programme by linking bonus outcomes to a set of company KPIs that include sustainability metrics. The bonus scheme uses seven of eight equally weighted KPIs (the “people and organisation” KPI based on employee feedback does not factor into the bonus), and includes sustainability-related KPIs such as safety (serious incidents per million work hours) and equity share scope 1 GHG intensity (kg CO2e/boe) [Source 1]. The company states that approximately 22% of the bonus potential is dependent on sustainability-related initiatives and targets, and that the bonus is paid to all permanent employees, including management, with the same share of bonus potential for all employees [Source 1]. Governance-wise, the Board’s Organisational Development and Compensation Committee (ODCC) is responsible for ensuring remuneration arrangements support the strategy, including sustainability matters, and it oversees the setting of targets and monitoring of progress related to KPIs linked to the incentive schemes for executive management team (EMT) remuneration [Source 2][Source 3].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide (i) key characteristics of the incentive scheme (bonus programme based on equally weighted KPIs and initiative/project delivery) and identify sustainability-related KPIs used (e.g., safety and scope 1 GHG intensity) [Source 1], and (ii) the proportion of bonus potential dependent on sustainability-related initiatives/targets (approx. 22%) [Source 1]. They also describe committee-level oversight (ODCC) for EMT incentive-linked KPIs and remuneration alignment with strategy/sustainability [Source 2][Source 3]. However, the evidence does not specify the exact sustainability targets/impacts used for remuneration assessment (beyond naming some KPIs), does not clearly state the approval/update level for the incentive scheme terms (e.g., BoD vs general meeting) and does not explicitly cover remuneration/incentives for the supervisory body/BoD members themselves [Source 1][Source 2][Source 3].
disclosure_gaps: Whether sustainability-related incentive/remuneration arrangements apply specifically to members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies (e.g., Board of Directors), versus employees/management generally; the passages only state the bonus is paid to all permanent employees including management [Source 1].
Specific sustainability-related targets and/or impacts used for performance assessment (e.g., target thresholds, time horizons, and which impacts), beyond listing example KPIs [Source 1].

Clear explanation of how sustainability metrics are used as performance benchmarks within remuneration policies for administrative/management/supervisory bodies (e.g., weighting per metric for EMT/BoD, scorecard mechanics) beyond the statement of equally weighted KPIs and 22% sustainability-related bonus potential [Source 1].

Proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability-related targets/impacts for each relevant body (e.g., EMT vs BoD), rather than an overall statement of ~22% of bonus potential [Source 1].
The level in the undertaking at which the terms of the incentive schemes are approved and updated (e.g., BoD, ODCC, general meeting) is not explicitly stated [Source 2][Source 3].
key_findings: Aker BP’s bonus scheme (variable remuneration) is driven by seven of eight equally weighted KPIs plus initiative/project delivery; the people & organisation KPI does not factor into the bonus [Source 1].
Sustainability-related KPIs included in the bonus framework include safety (serious incidents) and equity share scope 1 GHG intensity [Source 1].

Approximately 22% of bonus potential is dependent on sustainability-related initiatives and targets; the bonus is paid to all permanent employees, including management, with the same share of bonus potential for all employees [Source 1].

The ODCC is tasked with ensuring remuneration arrangements support the company strategy including sustainability matters, and it oversees target-setting and progress monitoring for KPIs linked to EMT incentive schemes [Source 2][Source 3].
